title: MCP servers can now ship skills, run tasks, and more with Claude
summary: MCP now lets servers work with Claude more like another agent, with Skills over MCP in public beta so servers can bundle guidance with their tools, loaded on demand and updated with the server. Tasks (background long-running jobs) and Elicitation (pausing to ask the user for input) are now generally available. File Uploads is rolling out soon so PDFs, spreadsheets, and images can reach servers without using the context window, and the update is part of an open spec that other compatible clients can use.

title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
summary: The beta Install as app option turns Claude artifacts into desktop apps with their own icon and window that open outside Claude and can be shared, with no API key or separate login needed. Access is permission-based, ranging from browser-level permissions to app features like notifications and menu bar to full computer access, and apps auto-update when the artifact is edited with permissions re-requested after updates. Apps are not reviewed by Anthropic, usage counts toward plan limits, and the feature is unavailable to HIPAA-ready organizations and hybrid deployments.

title: Using a "chaos loop" to harden the Claude Docs launch: 60 server errors across billions of requests
summary: Claude Docs, a collaborative editor for people and Claude sessions, launched September 16, 2026, and was hardened on staging with a "chaos loop" in which Claude ran load tests, read telemetry, proposed and deployed fixes, and reran tests, while humans approved irreversible changes. A copy-on-write fix cut a 3 GB document to about 180 MB and reduced pods from over 500 to about 50. The launch recorded about 2 billion requests, 60 server errors, no rollbacks, and 4.6 million documents created by September 22, at a cost of roughly $125,000 in inference.

title: How the Claude Code team thinks about verification
summary: Addy Osmani describes how the Claude Code team has coding agents verify their work with evidence, with about 90% of team code written and reviewed by Claude. The approach prioritizes end-to-end tests via a verify skill plus property and differential tests, turns recurring failures into hooks or CLAUDE.md rules, and includes safeguards such as bringing in a human after three failed fixes and starting gates in observe mode. Verification loops enable running dozens or hundreds of agents, and a separate grader improved success by up to 10 points.

title: Building strong safety evaluations
summary: Anthropic shares recommendations for building and relying on AI safety evaluations, drawing on psychology replication reforms. The approach shifts from counting refusals to an "appropriate response rate" over multi-turn conversations with a Claude-simulated user, and urges validating graders against human labels, preregistering analyses, and reporting uncertainty. Configuration matters, as a system prompt change moved one score from 60% on the API to 94% on claude.ai.

title: Introducing Claude Ship
summary: Claude Ship is a system for moving pull requests through review, fixes, and approval, combining Code Review (now GA) with the beta PR Steward and Claude Approvals. Claude repairs failing checks, merge conflicts, and reviewer feedback, and approves changes that a policy file permits, while /ship in Claude Code advances your own PRs once admins enable it per GitHub repo on Team and Enterprise plans. It is token-billed with admin spend limits, is unavailable with ZDR, HIPAA configuration, or customer-managed keys, and aims to remove the review and merge bottleneck as agents write more code.
